findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket (which stores reports and vendor data) are stored without SSE enforced by Terraform, relying on account-level defaults that may not exist.
This bucket stores ledger/financial export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
Versioning and access logging are configured, but no server_side_encryption_configuration is set, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, leaving operational runbooks (which may contain sensitive operational/credential procedures) unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL (the valid log-delivery grant is 'log-delivery-write'). This malformed value indicates the bucket's intended access control was not correctly applied, risking either deployment failure or, if resolved differently than intended, unintended write/read grants to this audit-log bucket.

None of the buckets in this configuration (reports_archive, ledger_exports, model_artifacts, ops_runbooks, audit_trail) have an associated aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, so there is no account/bucket-level guardrail preventing a future or accidental bucket policy or ACL change from making these buckets publicly accessible.

findings.issue_category: missing enforcement of encryption in transit
findings.description: No bucket policy denies non-TLS requests (e.g., aws:SecureTransport condition), so clients could interact with the audit-trail bucket over plain HTTP, allowing sensitive audit log data to be transmitted in cleartext.
